assumptions: All graphs and digraphs are finite and simple unless the statement explicitly says otherwise.

definitions.definition: A placement of vertices as points in R² together with polygonal obstacles P1,…,Pk such that two vertices are adjacent exactly when their connecting line segment intersects no obstacle.
The minimum k for which a graph has a k-obstacle drawing.

domain.description: Finite simple planar graphs and straight-line visibility drawings with finitely many polygonal obstacles.

quantifiers.domain: finite simple planar graphs with obstacle number greater than 1
positive integers proposed as a universal upper bound

statement.text: Does there exist a finite planar graph with obstacle number greater than 1? Separately, does there exist a universal integer k such that every finite planar graph has obstacle number at most k?

title: Obstacle number of planar graphs
